title: Weak regularity descends from finite coefficient-subring polynomial localizations
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $R_0\subseteq R$ a finite type integer subring [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $f_1,\ldots,f_c\in R_0[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $Q$ a prime of $R[x]$. For every finite type integer subring $B$ containing $R_0$, contract $Q$ to $Q_B$ in $B[x]$. Suppose the coefficientwise images of $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ form a weakly regular sequence in $B[x]_{Q_B}$: each next element acts injectively on the preceding prefix quotient [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then their images form a weakly regular sequence in $R[x]_Q$.

proof.text: For an arbitrary index i and fraction x whose product by the next equation is in the prefix ideal, apply the finite-stage ideal-relation theorem to the list of the first i equations and the next equation. It returns a finite type coefficient subring B, a localization map phi compatible on polynomials, and y mapping to x with the same ideal relation at B.

Use hstage at B and the i-th regular_mod_prev field. Multiplication is injective on the quotient by the prefix ideal. For a commutative ring A, regularity on A/I is equivalent to cancellation a*y in I implies y in I: Mathlib isSMulRegular_quotient_iff_mem_of_smul_mem proves this equivalence after Ideal.mul_top. Therefore y belongs to the stage prefix ideal.

Apply Ideal.mem_map_of_mem phi to y. Ideal.map_ofList and List.map_take identify the image ideal with the ambient prefix ideal. The compatibility of phi with algebraMap and MvPolynomial.map_map identify every coefficientwise stage equation with the ambient equation. Since phi(y)=x, x belongs to the ambient prefix ideal. The cancellation equivalence proves regularity on this prefix quotient. There are no indices for an empty sequence.

proof_origin.place: Elementwise proof of the filtered-colimit multiplication argument: witness one relation over a finite coefficient stage, cancel there, and map its ideal membership back. The finite-stage witness is proved directly in the delivered module.

lean.statement:
theorem isWeaklyRegular_polynomial_local_of_finiteType_subrings
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (R₀ : Subring R)
    (hR₀ : Algebra.FiniteType ℤ R₀) {n c : ℕ}
    (f₀ : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R₀)
    (Q : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)) [Q.IsPrime]
    (hstage : ∀ (B : Subring R) (hB : R₀ ≤ B), Algebra.FiniteType ℤ B →
      IsWeaklyRegular
        (Localization.AtPrime (Q.comap (MvPolynomial.map B.subtype)))
        ((List.ofFn (fun i ↦ MvPolynomial.map (Subring.inclusion hB) (f₀ i))).map
          (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) B)
            (Localization.AtPrime (Q.comap (MvPolynomial.map B.subtype)))))) :
    IsWeaklyRegular (Localization.AtPrime Q)
      ((List.ofFn (fun i ↦ MvPolynomial.map R₀.subtype (f₀ i))).map
        (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (Localization.AtPrime Q)))
